[docs/troubleshooting.md#installation-and-tooling]
**`pip install failed while vendoring dependencies`** : For vendoring providers (aws, alibaba, ibm, digitalocean, tencent, huawei), pskit downloads **Linux** wheels (`manylinux2014_<arch>`, `--only-binary=:all:`) for the target Python version. A package with no such wheel fails. Fixes: - pin a version that publishes manylinux wheels; - add flags with `package.pip_args`; - for pure-Python packages, check that they ship a wheel at all.

[docs/troubleshooting.md#security-notes]
- 500 responses never include exception details unless `PSKIT_DEBUG` is set. - `.env`, Terraform state and `pskit*.yml` are excluded from bundles. `.pskit/` is git-ignored. - `auth: none` routes are public. Embedded workflow orchestrators get a public `POST /workflows/<name>` route unless you set `options.http: false`. - `resources:` connection values are function environment variables: they land in Terraform state and, on premises, in `pskit_host.json`. Pass the *name* of a secret variable instead of the secret ([resources.md](resources.md#secrets)). - On premises, set `admin_token` when the host binds beyond loopback: it guards `/__pskit/*` (queues, invoke, workflows, executions, logs, stats). `pskit dashboard --serve` binds loopback and never sends that token to the browser. - Created AWS buckets block public access. Prefer a least-privilege `iam.statements` over `"*"` resources. - Keep secrets out of YAML: use `${env:...}` in CI or a secret manager via `${tf:...}`. - Report vulnerabilities privately (see `SECURITY.md` in the repository root).
